statements.text: Multiplying numerator and denominator by $2$ gives $\dfrac{6}{10}$, an equivalent fraction for the same quantity of that sandwich.
Changing only the numerator to $6$ and keeping the denominator $5$ still gives an equivalent fraction for that sandwich.
Equivalence requires first converting $\dfrac{3}{5}$ into a decimal.

stem:
Arjun has the fraction $\dfrac{3}{5}$ of a sandwich. He wants another fraction for the same quantity of that sandwich.

Which statements are correct?

teacher.key_rationale: Same nonzero factor on numerator and denominator yields an equivalent fraction on the same whole; 6/10 works. Statement 2 changes only the numerator. Statement 3 pulls in decimal conversion outside this hinge.
